finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::only `nan` is treated as a missing `issuedat`; a zero/epoch or absurdly-old timestamp is accepted and silently produces a no-op update
evidence: Verified at yorkie-event.controller.ts:56-58: the only guard is `Number.isNaN(issuedMs)`, so a parseable epoch-zero or Go zero-time (`0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`) yields a huge negative ms that passes `Math.min(issuedMs, now)`. `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt` (document.service.ts:119-122) uses `where: { updatedAt: { lt: at } }`, which can never match rows backfilled to `createdAt` by migration 20260710000000, and the controller still returns `{ ok: true }` so Yorkie won't retry — a silent drop. The claim's cited precedent is accurate: `parseTimestamp` in yorkie-admin.service.ts guards `Number.isNaN(ms) || ms <= 0` for exactly this "Yorkie unset" case, so the new parser is inconsistent with the repo's own handling. I could not confirm from source whether yorkie 0.7.12 actually emits a zero `issuedAt` (upstream Go not in the checkout), and impact is bounded (stale ordering only, self-healing on the next good event), hence minor with medium confidence.
